question: What is the average height of inner Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6000 metres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The average height of the Inner Himalayas is 6000 meters__.
 
• Greater Himalayas
 __
 
• It is also called as Inner Himalayas or Himadri.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks.
 
• The average height of these peaks is 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all prominent Himalayan peaks.
 
• The core of this part of the Himalayas is composed of granite.
 
• It is perennially snowbound, and a number of glaciers descend from this range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Himachal or Lesser Himalayas

 
 
• This range lies to the south of the Himadri and forms the most rugged mountain system.
 
• The ranges are mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is of 50 Km.
 
• Pir Panjal, the Dhaula Dhar and the Mahabharat ranges are important ranges in the Himalayas.
 
• This range consists of the famous valley of Kashmir, the Kangra and the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• This region is well-known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• Shivalik Range
 
 
• It is the outermost range of the Himalayas.
 
• They extend over a width of 10-50 Km and have an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The longitudinal valley lying between lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks is known as Duns.
 
• Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun are some of the well-known Duns
